question: A project lead notices that three colleagues each re-explain the same programme background to Claude every week in their own chats. What should she do first?
options: A) Ask each colleague to summarise their chats weekly and circulate those summaries by email.
B) Ask each colleague to keep one very long chat open so their own context accumulates over time.
C) Ask Claude to remember the programme background so nobody has to supply it again in future.
D) Gather the background the team keeps repeating into one agreed set of reference documents.
correct_answers: D) Gather the background the team keeps repeating into one agreed set of reference documents.
explanations: Incorrect. Circulating summaries adds manual work each week without giving Claude the background in any of the chats.
Incorrect. Very long personal chats condense their own history and draw more heavily on usage allowance, and the context stays siloed.
Incorrect. A chat does not carry context to colleagues' conversations; shared background has to be persisted deliberately.
Correct. Before choosing where to put shared context, the team needs to agree what that context actually is. A single reference set is what any later Project or hand-off will be built from.
